headline: Voted unanimously to notify Mayor Squailia of Elm Street ramp disrepair and loose bricks on Grove Street.
summary: Silvio’s Masonry and Landscaping finished the $37K repointing of bricks at the Wallace Avenue entrance without a permit. The Historical Commission denied a Certificate of Non-Applicability for the work. The Mayor’s second budget presentation reduced the COA building and grounds line by $12K.
decisions: Approved the June 11, 2026 meeting minutes, as amended, by unanimous vote.
A Certificate of Non-Applicability was denied for the repointing of bricks at the Wallace Avenue entrance.
Voted unanimously to notify Mayor Squailia of safety concerns about the Elm Street ramp and loose bricks at the rear of the Grove Street building.
The Fitchburg City Council rejected the initial FY27 COA budget request of $32K for building and grounds.
Approved moving the March 11, 2027 meeting to March 18, 2027, at 1:00 pm, with no objections.

plain_text:
FITCHBURG COUNCIL on AGING 
September 10, 2026 MEETING MINUTES 
 
PRESENT: Joe Byrne, Anne Fitch, Eleanor Zichelle, Margaret Padovano, Debbie Dion, Nancy Donohue, 
George Bourque, Tom Hopkins, Amanda Koeck, and Andrew Van Hazinga (left at 1:45 pm) EXCUSED 
ABSENCE: Todd Goodwin and Jim Craigen UNEXCUSED ABSENCE: Bonnie Hautala and Rev. Annie Belmer 
 
Vice Chair Byrne called the meeting to order at 1:02 pm and a QUORUM of eight was present. The 
meeting took place in the Fireplace Room at the Fitchburg Senior Center. 
 
PUBLIC COMMENT:  None 
 
MINUTES from the June 11, 2026, meeting were emailed to Board members. Hopkins motioned and Fitch 
seconded his motion to approve those minutes. Discussion: Dion thanked Goodwin and Craigen for 
recording the minutes on May 14, 2026, and June 11, 2026, due to her absence. Dion requested that her 
absences on  those dates be recognized as Excused Absences. The motion was amended to include 
Dion’s request. There was no further discussion and the amended motion received unanimous support. 
 
CHAIRPERSON’S REPORT:  None 
 
EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR’S REPORT:  Amanda Koeck *Silvio’s Masonry and Landscaping of Fitchburg has 
completed the $37K project involving the repointing of bricks at the main entrance on Wallace Avenue. 
The Historical Commission noted a recognizable difference between the old mortar and the new mortar. 
A Certificate of Non-Applicability was denied. Koeck reported the contractor did not get a permit to do 
the project. Perhaps the mortar mismatch could have been avoided through the permit protocol. Van 
Hazinga noted that municipal jobs are often exempt from securing a permit. Koeck stated the driving 
force behind the repointing project was to ensure safe points of building ingress and egress. 
 
*Piggybacking on the aforementioned repointing project, Donohue initiated a brief discussion about the 
state of disrepair of the Elm Street ramp and the surrounding sidewalk area. It was also noted that the 
COA continues to have grave concern about the remaining loose bricks in the rear of the building on 
Grove Street. Bourque motioned and Fitch seconded his motion to notify Mayor Squailia of these safety 
concerns. Van Hazinga suggested the importance of including the Municipal Facilities Director in this 
communication. Koeck reported that she already plans to submit a grant application next year to focus 
on ramp safety improvements and the possibility of installing an awning above the Elm Street entrance. 
Bourque’s motion received unanimous support. 
 
*Koeck provided an update on the FY27 COA budget. The initial budget request totaled $32K for building 
and grounds, and was included in the Mayor’s first presentation of the City’s Operating Budget. The 
Fitchburg City Council rejected that budget. In the Mayor’s second presentation of the City’s Operating 
Budget the COA building and grounds line was reduced by $12K. Koeck noted that heat and electricity are 
separate budget items. Please note: You can view the FY27 COA budget on page 40 in the FY27 city 
budget. 
 
*Koeck informed the Board that Monty Tech will no longer be able to deliver the Armory Cafe meals. 
Thank you to Dana Jones, Kitchen Coordinator, for his willingness to pick up the meals at Monty Tech. 
Unanimously approved at Oct 10, 2026 COA meeting.
Koeck said Formula Grant funding will be used to pay Jones for his time and mileage. A suggested 
donation of $3.00 from those diners able to pay would be greatly appreciated to help defray the cost of 
meals. 
 
*A new format was used in the September 2026, edition of Fitchburg Senior Focus. The newsletter was a 
Microsoft publication in the past. Thank you to Elyse Miles and Carol Cotnoir for learning how to use 
Canva for the publication of the current newsletter. Thank you to the Friends for paying any postage fees. 
Envelopes are funded by the Formula Grant. Thank you to Van Hazinga for lauding the newsletter. 
 
*Allyson Chalapatas, Certified Dementia Practitioner, will commence the Memory Cafe at the Fitchburg 
Senior Center. The program will be held at 2:00 pm on the second Tuesday of the month starting in 
October 2026. 
 
*The Center for Social and Demographic Research at UMass Boston would like the Fitchburg Senior 
Center to participate in their data collection. They currently serve over 60 municipalities and they offered 
to do a Zoom presentation for the Board. Since there is a fee to participate in their research, the Board 
wants to know the advantage of our participation prior to making a commitment to this project. Koeck 
will reach out to the Senior Center in Littleton, MA. Bourque suggested requesting pertinent literature 
from UMass Boston. 
 
* Koeck requested Board approval to change the date of our March 11, 2027, meeting. There were no 
objections and the NEW DATE for the Board meeting is March 18, 2027, at 1:00 pm. 
 
OLD BUSINESS:  Amanda Koeck 
Koeck reported there has been no update from City Hall on the reappointments of Board members 
Goodwin, Byrne, Craigen, Padovano, and Rev. Belmer. Please be reminded that Mayor Squailia informed 
Koeck that they may continue to serve as COA Board members as they await their official 
reappointments. 
 
NEW BUSINESS:  None 
 
COMMUNICATION:  None 
 
BOARD COMMENT:  None 
 
NEXT MEETING:  Thursday, October 8, 2026 at 1:00 pm 
 
ADJOURNMENT:  Hopkins motioned to adjourn and Padovano seconded his motion. No discussion 
followed and there was a unanimous vote to adjourn at 1:50 pm. 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
Debbie Dion 
Recording Secretary
